record_notes.DCP-LETT-1438: June 25, supplied 1851, complete four-page ALS. Eight retained blocks, five footnotes and bibliography read. Requests re-loan of the previously returned Sertularia/Plumularia to inspect Scalpellum attachment; later published anatomical conclusion not yet this request. Image fossil was absent on earlier inquiry, current Geological Society custody only a possibility. Publication complaint distinguishes delayed society distribution from previously received advance copies; September receipt in apparatus remains later. Address and signature are retained blocks, not eight substantive paragraphs. No incoming Bowerbank text preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1455: September 28, supplied 1851, complete four-page ALS. Six blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Sowerby reports ten plates ready for printing, not completed printing. Fire motivates request for payment of £23 10s; postscript changes plan to Darwin advancing money and later taking the society cheque. October 1 loan entry and October 6 society payment are later outcomes, not accomplished on September 28. Correcting page 200, missing society publications only presumed published. No Sowerby report or Bowerbank reply text supplied.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1420: Friday assigned April 25, 1851, three-page ALS from Susan; salutation addresses Charles and Emma although metadata recipient is Charles. Five blocks, no editorial footnotes. Susan received two Fanny letters this morning, Charles letter yesterday after missed post; under assigned date April 25 and April 24 respectively, not Charles receipt of this Susan letter. Catherine ill since Sunday evening and unable to travel; Susan says she might have gone to Malvern had she known. Grief, prayer and affection are Susan voice, not Charles beliefs. No preserved current Charles letter supplies the antecedent; family subject is eligible in principle.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1467: Signed autograph draft dated October 1855 through May 1856, crossing period boundary. Thirteen retained blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Cattell provided introduction permission, not a surviving Fairbeard prompt. Pea planting is this past summer; exact writing, dispatch and receipt unknown. Entire cover letter crossed in pencil, verso questions not crossed. Raw HTML inspected: literal diag/ramme markers and paragraph breaks, no image/table encoding. Four visible numbered question groups occur in order 2,1,4,3, despite editorial summary saying five questions; do not fabricate a fifth item or silently reorder. Questions concern stability, proximity/crossing, selection over generations and relative variety variability. Later Natural selection answer with blank correspondent name is apparatus evidence, not surviving contemporaneous Fairbeard reply or permission to backdate knowledge. Rendering and exact-date hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1387: January 24, supplied 1851, four-page ALS. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Proof-plate comparison completed, no damage while with Sowerby; earlier shipping injury and authorized removal from chalk acknowledged. About half packed this morning; all to be sent by Wednesday absent contrary message, not proof shipped/arrived. Duplicate donation conditional, intended British Museum destination; later catalogue absence does not prove donation at this date. Fitch prior notes absent, same-author correspondence continuity not a prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1799: December 24, 1855, one-page Gordon ALS. Three blocks, four footnotes, separate Darwin annotations and bibliography. Beaton seedlings initially grew, failed to form roots and died; other stated Brunsvigia/Vallota cross produced two bulbs. Darwin pencil taxon additions (including Amaryllis over Vallota) and portfolio mark are separate undated layer, not Gordon original wording. Later 1868 discussion cannot supply contemporary receipt date or missing question. No current Darwin endpoint preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1567: April 26, supplied 1854, one-page ALS. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Explicit thanks for Grove notification of Philosophical Club election, known by this writing. April 24 election and Grove replaced as treasurer by Hooker are apparatus, not incoming notification wording. Hooker March request and Grove notice are distinct communications; no preserved Grove incoming found. Social esteem belongs in persona evidence but does not establish a textual pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1584: Damaged three-page Babington ALS, approximately June 1855, not exact June 1 or June 30. Six surviving blocks, five extensive footnotes, Darwin annotations and bibliography. Babington answers Darwin paper, regards three Primula forms as distinct species, calycantha as cultivation changes; damaged health and completed cirripede-work remarks remain incomplete. Verbascum cream colour and Isle of Wight yellow report attributed to Arnott, final two lines absent. Footnote 2 actually reproduces Darwin questions and Babington written additions preserved in Gärtner book: separate mixed-voice witness, not entirely missing enclosure and not a catalogued Darwin letter here. Original inserted paper not inspected; dates of its questions/replies and letter receipt unproved. Darwin marginal conclusions undated; later books/papers not contemporary answer text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1393: March 4, supplied 1851, four-page ALS. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Last proof finished, specimens being returned with catalogue not transcribed here; safe arrival hoped only. Two species named, other young material insufficient to name; unique P. semilatus and few S. tuberculatum mean no actual duplicate donation request/receipt. Scarcity prevents what Darwin otherwise would have asked. Earlier Harris loans and missing cover letters distinct from current proof completion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-363: Fresh earlier context: July 1, 1837 Babington ALS. Three blocks and two footnotes. Returned yesterday evening and found Darwin letter, establishing in-hand by June 30 without precise delivery. Preliminary worldwide water-insect inventory, descriptions incomplete; Australian species promised for Hope next week, others after vacation, route via Darwin or Waterhouse proposed. Entomological Society publication conditional on Darwin preference. Later 1838 paper and 1841–43 print do not prove current completed descriptions; missing Darwin prompt not reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-708: Fresh earlier context: October 26, 1843 Babington ALS. Five blocks and two footnotes. Examined and returns Kemp Atriplex, confidently A. angustifolia variety with rich-soil analogues; A. hastata distinct, Henslow A. patula material still desired. Soil history of this specific plant inferred from appearance, not observed cultivation. Enclosure sent, Darwin receipt not dated. Prior Henslow correspondence is other-author context, not a current 1855 Primula prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1145: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Only torn opening phrase, family valediction and Susan signature survive. Cannot reconstruct subject or make it the request for Malvern diary in1234. Assigned1848? is based on Darwin reused-paper notes quoting March4 and August19,1848 Athenaeum pages about Forbes genera continuity. Article publication dates constrain earliest possible annotations, not Susan original composition or an exact receipt. Darwin notes in footnote2 are original historical text, distinct from Susan voice and not safely contemporaneous with letter. No precise activation date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1234: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Monday editorial March19,1849. Answers missing Susan request for hydropathic diary. P1–5 Darwin: timed washing/walking/compress/diet/footbaths, self-reported stronger despite sickness, tomorrow planned packing, faithless compliance with homeopathy, Gully opinion, snuff concession, indolence and grief for father. Raw MathML gives quarter before7 (6:45) and1½ hours, not14 and12. Gully pathology is attributed historical opinion; later routines/May changes are not current facts. P6 is explicitly in Emma hand and reports Annie/MissThorley conversation, not Charles prose. Potential sharing with Parkers is a request, not proof of forwarding.1145 valediction contains no diary prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-833: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh prior context: Wednesday conjecturalNovember27,1844, broader editorial span afterOctober1844 visit and beforeMarch1845 purchase agreement. Thanks two business notes, father advice, household gifts and asks Susan visit. Encloses two missing Higgins notes, considers Lincolnshire land conditional on father approval and reports oral Lubbock advice. LaterMarch1845estate proposal839 is not interchangeable with these earlier notes. No final purchase or guaranteed particular estate identified; previous primary holds preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-913: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh prior context: copied September3–4,1845 letter, XMLwhen onlySeptember3 despite explicit Thursday morning startP3. P1–2September3 family health, railway dividends, budgets and garden plans; P3September4 servants room/passage needs, Cresy proposed building cost and reported village disputes. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1325: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 5 with supplied 1850 year. Two more specimens safely received, valves new to Fitch collection but unsuitable as basis for specific names. New-to-collection does not mean new species. No incoming cover text preserved and no precise arrival time beyond acknowledgment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1366: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 3 with supplied 1850 year. Explicitly answers missing Fitch inquiry over long retention, states delay caused by engravings and asks continued loan. Artist progress partly known, much merely hoped; prior engagements/Botanic Garden routine are hypothesized causes. Council members also urged progress. No completed plates or returned collection yet, and prior permission cannot be inferred to extend indefinitely. Missing Fitch query and Sowerby reports preclude a textual pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1369: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 11 with supplied 1850 year. Fitch note and Sowerby complaint response arrived by same post; one of five plates perfect, not all five. Sowerby reports house demolition as chief cause, a newly supplied explanation rather than Darwin earlier knowledge. Darwin plans further pressure and says Fitch will soon demand specimens back. Pamphlet received but title is editorial possibility, not certain identification or proof read. Declines additional specimens. Sowerby is James de Carle; later George Brettingham Jr work on other volumes does not change authorship of this report.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1376: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Monday, conjectural December 1850. Several specimens with excellent drawings back from Sowerby, several still retained, all plate positions arranged but proof verification pending. Promises Fitch return in week completed proofs checked; no actual return date follows. Dating rationale places between November 11, 1850 and January 24, 1851, with completed illustrations by middle January only described in later context. Preferred December month is not independently established; keep exact-date and active-period-boundary hold rather than exclude possible early 1851. No fresh incoming prompt or complete proofs supplied here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1305A: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. February 25 with supplied 1850 year supported by cancellation-code window and damaged February 26 postmark. Found dry/spirit sponges, offers them and intends leaving at Geological Society next Thursday, February 28, not proof actual dispatch or personal London visit. Further specimens believed present but cannot be found. Plumularia return statement refers specimen acknowledged in 1229, same-author loan continuity rather than QA. Later June 1851 request to re-examine remains future. Bowerbank later monograph and absent acknowledgment do not negate historical gift.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1310: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Friday evening conjectured March 8, 1850 from March 17 follow-up; apparatus excludes March 15 only as probably insufficient time for response, not logically impossible. Exact-date hold retained. Misdirected missing letter travelled via Farnham and arrived yesterday; do not turn relative day into securely March 7. Loan specimen includes presumed new Chthamalus and B. cranchii; later taxonomy remains separate. Offers purchase or retention as loan, payment completed only by later 1312 stamps. Society acceptance now heard, drawings/MS still being prepared. Copper engraving required for growth lines; Sowerby drawing already under way but engraving preference not completed commission. Hanley address still requested; membership only supposed, not proved admission.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1312: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 17 with supplied 1850 year independently supported by copyist-recorded March 18 postmark. Missing Bowerbank response supplies Hanley address requested in 1310. Visit to Hanley prospective when next in London, not accomplished here. Enclosed stamps pay for Eling specimen, resolving earlier loan/purchase option, but no actual delivery of stamps or Hanley meeting inferred. Logistics is eligible correspondence in principle, but missing prompt precludes pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1382F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday assigned April 24, 1850 from council meeting Friday April 26. Circular received this morning announces meeting, does not grant permission. Requests eight foreign species openly included in small type, supported by reported oral views of Forbes, Morris and Flower; actual April 26 funding/permission in minutes is later editorial outcome. Sponge bottle sent last Thursday, April 18 under assigned date; recipient receipt explicitly queried, not established. Charlesworth report of Pearce recovery is attributed historical information; Darwin approach to Pearce unanswered and fossil examination not done. Preserve current concinus spelling, separately note later concinnus if needed. No circular, Charlesworth communication or Pearce response text survives here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1344: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 6, supplied 1850. Missing Harris note of August 2 known, fossils classified this morning and numbered; many valves unnamed because condition or nondiagnostic anatomy. Numbered list skips 4, repeats 7 to across blocks and includes do, alternatives and question marks; raw paragraphs not a table. New forms partly too immature to name, generic assignment tentative. Original chalk beds unknown, broad upper-chalk affinity only inference. More specimens requested by August 18, return and describing planned for 18/19; later journal records actual return August 16, not current knowledge or correction of intention.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
